page: The Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd5 is a bare-metal server designed for memory-intensive enterprise computing. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9255 processor operating at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz, the system delivers 24 physical cores and 48 execution threads under a dedicated allocation scheme. It features a cache architecture comprising 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 384 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB memory ratio per thread. Local storage is provided through a bundled 960 GB NVMe solid-state drive, complemented by one included public IPv4 address without integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place this bare-metal platform within top-tier percentiles for raw execution and compiler tasks. Single-core stress-ng tests reach 3629.78 points, and the Geekbench single-core score of 2742.0 ranks in the top ten percent of cloud platforms, paired with a multi-core score of 25509.0. Clang compilation speed registers 59880.0, highlighting responsiveness during heavy build routines. In memory workloads, cached 16 KB read bandwidth achieves 5282.07 GB/sec, while large uncached 256 MB block reads sustain 205.04 GB/sec. Uncached write bandwidth moderates to 88.06 GB/sec. Data throughput is underscored by 102.69 GB/sec in static web serving and 84.77 million operations per second during Redis SET transactions, bolstered by AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 vector extensions.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture removes hypervisor virtualization penalties and guarantees predictable CPU resource access across all 48 threads. The substantial DDR5 memory capacity per core accommodates memory-bound workloads that would otherwise require multiple smaller virtual instances. A potential architectural tradeoff is the moderate local storage footprint of 960 GB relative to the heavy 384 GB memory pool, making it dependent on networked storage or external databases for data volumes exceeding local disk limits. The system is well configured for in-memory caching layers, Redis instances, heavy compilation pipelines, and data analytics engines.
description: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd5 is a memory-optimized bare-metal server configured with a dedicated 24-core, 48-thread AMD EPYC 9255 processor running at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 384 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation that excels in memory-intensive operations. Storage is provided by a bundled 960 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. Without GPU hardware, this platform targets pure central processing tasks, supported by instruction set extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16. Benchmark assessments demonstrate top-tier execution across single-core compute, clang software compilation, text processing, and static web serving throughput exceeding 100 GB/s. Memory performance remains strong with read bandwidth exceeding 200 GB/s on large blocks. The high RAM-to-core ratio and dedicated compute allocation make this machine suited for in-memory databases, large Redis deployments, data analytics, and continuous integration pipelines.
